knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Area of a Triangle

question.:question/problem:
![](images/30/3099b3b3932e30ebeb67b908e131aa296785dccf530d8f2076f23ce0cb819eaf.png)

Find the area of $△ABC.$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}с & =AB=3, \\ b & =AC=7, \\ m∠A & ={128}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{128}^{∘}=0.788\,010,
$$

rounded to six decimal places,  we calculate the area as follows:
 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 7\cdot 3\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{128}^{∘} \\  & =10.5\cdot (0.788\,010) \\  & ≈8.27,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Area of a Triangle

question.:question/problem:
![](images/77/77419eacd4ad3c33252b635ad4763ab21c5a2c9072b18f098340efead5a1e12e.png)

Find the area of $\triangle ABC$, in square units. Round your answer to **two decimal places**.

> Use a scientific calculator in degree mode.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The sides $CA=9$ and $CB=13$ meet at $C$, so $37^{\circ}$ is their included angle. Use

$$
\mathcal A=\frac12(CA)(CB)\sin C.
$$

Substituting gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal A&=\frac12(9)(13)\sin 37^{\circ}\\
&=58.5\sin 37^{\circ}\\
&=35.20617885\ldots\\
&\approx35.21.
\end{aligned}
$$

The area is $35.21$ square units. Keep the calculator's full precision until the final rounding.

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Area of a Triangle

question.:question/problem:
![](images/9f/9f5c8eff55cd477831f43d3d8508ca76c4f428dba474c1f68b84ff76b571ff10.png)

$E$ lies on $BC$. The two marked angles at $A$ are $\angle BAE=24^{\circ}$ and $\angle EAC=30^{\circ}$.

Rounded to **two decimal places**, the area of $\triangle ABC$ is {{field-1}} square units.

> Use a scientific calculator in degree mode.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The included angle between $AB=8$ and $AC=11$ is the whole angle $\angle BAC$, not either marked part. Add the adjacent angles:

$$
\angle BAC=24^{\circ}+30^{\circ}=54^{\circ}.
$$

Use these two sides and their included angle:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal A&=\frac12(AB)(AC)\sin(\angle BAC)\\
&=\frac12(8)(11)\sin54^{\circ}\\
&=44\sin54^{\circ}\\
&=35.59674775\ldots\\
&\approx35.60.
\end{aligned}
$$

The area is $35.60$ square units. Using only $24^{\circ}$ or $30^{\circ}$ with sides $AB$ and $AC$ would pair those sides with the wrong angle.

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Area of a Triangle

question.:question/problem:
![](images/6c/6caafe3e5db48af9acf0fe404d10eadc112fb1b9dc4e3b9a62aafad234b7fef2.png)

$E$ lies on $AB$. The two marked angles at $C$ are $\angle BCE=28^{\circ}$ and $\angle ECA=40^{\circ}$. The side lengths are $CA=x+2$ and $CB=2x$, and $CA+CB=23$. All lengths use the same unit.

Rounded to **two decimal places**, the area of $\triangle ABC$ is {{field-1}} square units.

> Use a scientific calculator in degree mode.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First determine the two side lengths. Their sum is $23$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
(x+2)+2x&=23\\
3x+2&=23\\
x&=7.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $CA=x+2=9$ and $CB=2x=14$.

The included angle between these sides is the whole angle $\angle ACB$. Add its two marked parts:

$$
\angle ACB=28^{\circ}+40^{\circ}=68^{\circ}.
$$

Now apply the triangle area formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal A&=\frac12(CA)(CB)\sin(\angle ACB)\\
&=\frac12(9)(14)\sin68^{\circ}\\
&=63\sin68^{\circ}\\
&=58.41258283\ldots\\
&\approx58.41.
\end{aligned}
$$

The area is $58.41$ square units. Use the side lengths $9$ and $14$, rather than $x$ itself. Both the side expressions and the two angle markings must be combined before substituting into the formula.
